lessons.title: Computer hardware
lessons.description: Hardware is the physical equipment in a computer. A microprocessor carries out CPU instructions. The Internet connects networks worldwide; mobile computing supports portable communication; AI performs tasks such as learning, reasoning, and problem solving.

notes.title: Hardware fundamentals
notes.body: Hardware is the physical equipment in a computer. A microprocessor carries out CPU instructions. The Internet connects networks worldwide; mobile computing supports portable communication; AI performs tasks such as learning, reasoning, and problem solving.

notes.title: CPU and motherboard
notes.body: The CPU executes instructions, calculations, and logic. Multiple cores allow concurrent work. The motherboard connects the CPU, RAM, storage, and peripherals through buses, slots, and connectors. BIOS/UEFI firmware initializes hardware during startup.

notes.title: RAM versus storage
notes.body: RAM holds data currently needed by the CPU and is volatile: its contents are lost when power is removed. Storage retains data across shutdowns. More RAM can help multitasking when memory capacity is the bottleneck.

notes.title: HDD versus SSD
notes.body: An HDD uses spinning magnetic platters. An SSD uses flash memory and has no moving parts. SSDs typically improve startup and file access speeds; HDDs are commonly chosen for capacity at lower cost.

notes.title: Power supply
notes.body: The PSU converts AC from the wall into low-voltage DC for computer components. Capacity is measured in watts. Choose capacity for the whole system. 80 Plus ratings describe efficiency; modular cabling helps cable management.

notes.title: Graphics processing
notes.body: The GPU renders images, video, and animation. Integrated graphics handle basic tasks; dedicated graphics cards support demanding work such as gaming, video editing, and 3D rendering.

notes.title: Cooling
notes.body: Heatsinks absorb and dissipate heat; fans move air. Cooling keeps the CPU, GPU, and other components within safe operating temperatures. Some high-performance systems use liquid cooling.

notes.title: Input and output
notes.body: Input devices send information into a computer: keyboard, mouse, microphone, and scanner. Output devices present information: monitor, speakers, headphones, and printer.

lessons.title: Administrator roles
lessons.description: System administration keeps computer systems and related services reliable and usable. It combines technical support, efficient resource use, permissions, monitoring, upgrades, and maintenance to meet service-quality goals.

notes.title: Purpose of system administration
notes.body: System administration keeps computer systems and related services reliable and usable. It combines technical support, efficient resource use, permissions, monitoring, upgrades, and maintenance to meet service-quality goals.

notes.title: Database administrator
notes.body: A DBA manages database integrity, reliability, access, backup, restoration, and troubleshooting. Useful skills include SQL, operating systems, analysis, organization, communication, and problem solving.

notes.title: Network administrator
notes.body: A network administrator installs and maintains routers, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and network services. They resolve connectivity issues and protect access. LAN, WAN, VPN, and SAN knowledge supports this role.

notes.title: Security administrator
notes.body: Security administrators protect systems and sensitive data, establish policies, identify weak points, manage defenses, and respond to intrusions. Identity management controls who can access information; intrusion detection flags suspicious activity.

notes.title: Security skills
notes.body: Vulnerability assessment examines weaknesses; risk management identifies, evaluates, and addresses threats. Communication, critical thinking, continuous learning, and calm under pressure support effective incident response.

notes.title: Web and server administrator
notes.body: Web administrators maintain services such as Apache or IIS, manage website deployment and security, maintain site databases, and respond to user support issues. Coding, database, design, project management, and teamwork skills are useful.

notes.title: Routine responsibilities
notes.body: Administrators inspect systems, back up data, apply updates, configure hardware and software, manage user accounts, answer technical questions, troubleshoot, and keep networks available. Documenting system configuration supports later maintenance.

lessons.description: Network and system administration manages the operation of human–computer systems. The purpose is to help users accomplish work while considering the benefit of the whole community.

notes.title: Human–computer systems
notes.body: Network and system administration manages the operation of human–computer systems. The purpose is to help users accomplish work while considering the benefit of the whole community.

notes.title: Technology in its environment
notes.body: Hardware configurations and software configurations serve users. Hardware needs suitable power, temperature, and standards. Administration must account for physical constraints as well as software behavior.

notes.title: The human role
notes.body: Effective administration requires patience, understanding, knowledge, and experience. Administrators combine diagnosis, user support, repair, and prevention while balancing competing needs.

notes.title: Planning and scale
notes.body: Challenges include logical network design, upgradeable deployments, selecting services, adequate security, user comfort, error recovery, and keeping knowledge current. Installing an operating system is only one part of the job.

notes.title: Interdependence
notes.body: Even when responsible only for individual computers, an administrator needs to understand data flow and how one machine affects others. Local changes can influence the wider network community.

notes.title: Computer ethics
notes.body: Respect others’ work, privacy, resources, and intellectual output. Do not use computers to harm, steal, deceive, or interfere. Use resources with authorization, honor software licensing, and consider the social consequences of programs.

notes.title: Bugs and unexpected behavior
notes.body: Systems can exhibit bugs or unplanned interactions. Causes include poor quality control, operating system problems, incompatible software, and attacks. Administrators need evidence, adaptability, and practical workarounds.

lessons.source: DIAGNOSTICS, FAULT AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT - GROUP 2.pdf
lessons.description: Diagnostics investigates a problem to determine its cause. Identify the symptom, collect information, analyze evidence, identify the cause, apply a solution, and verify the result. A visible symptom can have several possible causes.

notes.title: Diagnostics: investigate
notes.body: Diagnostics investigates a problem to determine its cause. Identify the symptom, collect information, analyze evidence, identify the cause, apply a solution, and verify the result. A visible symptom can have several possible causes.

notes.title: Evidence before action
notes.body: Use logs, error messages, monitoring data, network status, performance statistics, configuration records, and user reports. Compare evidence to distinguish the actual cause from plausible alternatives.

notes.title: Fault versus failure
notes.body: A fault is the underlying defect or condition. A failure is the resulting loss of function or service. Examples of faults include damaged cables, incorrect settings, corrupted data, failed components, or insufficient storage.

notes.title: Fault management: restore
notes.body: Detect, isolate, diagnose, correct, restore service, and monitor. The goal is normal operation with minimal impact on users. Verify recovery rather than assuming that an attempted fix succeeded.

notes.title: Temporary and long-term fixes
notes.body: Safely removing unnecessary temporary data can restore a full server. Repeatedly doing so may leave the underlying capacity problem unresolved. Monitoring, storage expansion, or changed data-management practices may be needed.

notes.title: Change management: control
notes.body: Plan, assess risk and impact, obtain approval, implement, test, and review changes. Prepare backups and a recovery plan. Updates, replacements, database changes, and network configuration changes can introduce unexpected effects.

notes.title: Types of change
notes.body: Standard changes are routine and follow established procedures. Normal changes require assessment and authorization. Emergency changes address critical situations where waiting for the normal process creates greater risk.

notes.title: Verification and the full cycle
notes.body: After implementation, test, monitor, document, and review the result. Diagnostics explains the problem; fault management restores operation; change management controls lasting improvements. Remember: investigate → restore → improve → verify.

lessons.title: Networked communities
lessons.description: A networked community connects people, devices, computer systems, and digital services so they can communicate, share resources, and collaborate. A university with students, staff, Wi-Fi, servers, and learning platforms is one example.

notes.title: A connected community
notes.body: A networked community connects people, devices, computer systems, and digital services so they can communicate, share resources, and collaborate. A university with students, staff, Wi-Fi, servers, and learning platforms is one example.

notes.title: People, devices, systems, services
notes.body: People use resources; devices connect them; systems manage data, accounts, and operations; services provide capabilities such as email and file sharing. Networks allow these elements to exchange information.

notes.title: Community types
notes.body: Educational networks connect students and learning systems. Business networks connect employees and company resources. Government networks connect offices. Online communities connect participants through platforms; cloud-based communities share internet-accessible applications and data.

notes.title: Key characteristics
notes.body: Connectivity links devices; communication exchanges information; resource sharing provides common files, printers, applications, or storage; collaboration supports joint work. Management may be centralized or decentralized. Accessibility depends on permissions and security.

notes.title: Connection methods
notes.body: Ethernet provides wired access. Wi-Fi provides wireless access. Mobile data uses cellular networks such as 4G or 5G. A VPN supports authorized access to a private network. Internet connections link services across locations.

notes.title: Challenges
notes.body: Downtime, cyberattacks, privacy risks, hardware/software problems, and incorrect settings can disrupt services. Some services depend on connectivity and become unavailable when the network or Internet fails.

notes.title: Administrator responsibilities
notes.body: Manage accounts and permissions, maintain servers and network services, install and configure systems, monitor performance, troubleshoot, secure data, and perform backup and recovery.

notes.title: Match the response to the problem
notes.body: Downtime: troubleshoot devices and restore connectivity. Unauthorized access: isolate affected accounts and strengthen controls. Data loss: restore backups. Malware: isolate, investigate, and update. Misconfiguration: identify and correct settings.

questions.prompt: Which component executes program instructions and calculations?

questions.explanation: The motherboard provides the main circuit board, buses, and connectors.

questions.prompt: Which device is an input device?

questions.prompt: Which device produces a physical copy of a document?

questions.prompt: Why is application data loaded into RAM while a program runs?

questions.prompt: What is the role of BIOS/UEFI during startup?

questions.prompt: What is the central purpose of system administration?

questions.explanation: System administration supports reliable operation, users, and service quality.

questions.prompt: Who primarily manages database integrity, backups, and restoration?

questions.prompt: Who primarily configures routers, switches, and VPNs?

questions.prompt: Which task belongs to identity management?

questions.prompt: Which skill focuses on flagging suspicious system activity?

questions.prompt: Which administrator maintains Apache or IIS web services?

questions.prompt: An employee cannot reach a shared service because of a router configuration. Which role is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Network administrators troubleshoot network connectivity and equipment.

questions.prompt: Which is a soft skill useful for a database administrator?
questions.explanation: Communication supports teamwork and explaining technical needs to others.

questions.prompt: Why should a system administrator document the system setup?
options: To support understanding and future maintenance
To eliminate the need for backups
To make every account an administrator
questions.explanation: Documenting the setup is an explicit system administration responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which action is a routine system administration responsibility?
questions.explanation: Account and permission management is part of system administration.

questions.prompt: What does risk management involve in security administration?
options: Guarantee that no software has bugs
Replace every firewall with a switch
questions.explanation: Risk management assesses threats and selects appropriate responses.

questions.prompt: Which professional habit helps a security administrator handle changing threats?
questions.explanation: The lesson emphasizes lifelong learning for security professionals.

questions.prompt: A website has a deployment, connectivity, or functionality issue. Which role commonly handles its help desk request?

questions.prompt: What is a DBA expected to do after data loss when a usable backup exists?

questions.prompt: Why are communication and teamwork useful to network administrators?

questions.explanation: Network administrators work with teams and users to keep systems available.

questions.prompt: Which role develops security policies and helps respond to unwanted intrusions?
questions.explanation: Security administrators establish protections and respond to threats.

questions.prompt: Network and system administration is concerned with which kind of operational management?

questions.prompt: Whose interests should an administrator consider beyond an individual user’s request?
questions.explanation: Administration should serve the community rather than just a few selfish needs.

questions.prompt: Which physical requirement matters when deploying computer hardware?

questions.prompt: Which set of qualities supports the human side of administration?

To prevent all users from working
To remove the need for power

questions.explanation: The lesson highlights the continually increasing amount of technical knowledge.

questions.explanation: The administrator should empower users while considering the greater community.

A failure always happens before any fault exists
questions.explanation: The lesson distinguishes an underlying condition from its service consequence.

options: Restore normal operation while minimizing user impact

options: Verify recovery and monitor the service
Assume success and delete all evidence
questions.explanation: Corrective action must be followed by verification and monitoring.

Delete a few temporary files each time without investigation
questions.explanation: A lasting response addresses recurring causes and capacity rather than only symptoms.

questions.prompt: What is change management?
options: A controlled process for assessing and implementing IT modifications
Any unrecorded edit to a server
questions.explanation: It includes planning, assessment, approval, implementation, and review.

questions.prompt: Before expanding a university database, which preparation is appropriate?
options: Assess impact, back up data, obtain approval, and prepare recovery
Change it immediately without a plan
questions.explanation: The source example describes controlled preparation for a storage expansion.

questions.explanation: The lesson defines a normal change by assessment and authorization.

questions.explanation: Emergency changes address urgent critical situations.

questions.prompt: Which response best matches a misconfiguration?

questions.prompt: Why does a networked community need a system administrator?
